needed_evidence: S1 London-wide ULEZ One Year Report, 'ULEZ impact analysis' section and Appendix 3: the method behind 'up to 4.8%' (DID vs modelled), the control sites used (outer London or outside Greater London), the meteorological adjustment, the central estimate, the confidence interval, and the number of outer London roadside sites.

npj Clean Air 2025 (Birmingham) Supplementary Tables S5/S6 and Fig. 3: the ULEZ3 effect estimate and Jackknife+ 95% interval specifically for outer London urban traffic sites, and the number of such sites.

npj Clean Air 2025 Supplementary Fig. S13 equivalent for ULEZ3: any announcement or anticipation test using a Nov 2022 or Jan 2023 (scrappage) cut-off, and the pre-period fit (RMSE) for the outer London traffic synthetic control.
Independent difference-in-differences of roadside NO2 at outer London LAQN/AURN sites against roadside sites in Kent, Essex, Surrey and Hertfordshire, Aug 2022-Aug 2024, meteorology-normalised.

TfL ANPR data for outer London only: compliance rate and non-compliant vehicle counts monthly 2022-2024, with the pre-announcement trend rate, plus TfL/DfT traffic counts for outer London over the same period.
Outer London 2024 annual mean NO2 at roadside/kerbside sites only (not pooled with background), to convert the 4.8% into µg/m3 correctly.
Any Imperial College or King's College analysis that independently estimates the outer London expansion effect, rather than deferring to the GLA report (S3 defers).

Independence note: S5 and S6 are the same study (PMC and Nature hosts). E17/E37, E21/E41, E26/E43, E24/E45 and E18/E38 should be one origin group, not two. A11's 'two independent copies' answer is wrong. E1 and E6 are also one origin (S2 relays S1).

summary.directive: C1 defeated_by: A3 is out because A26 (undermine) stands: The BBC relay drops two qualifiers. The primary report says 'roadside' and 'up to 4.8 per cent' (E1). E6 reports a flat '4.8% lower' for 'NO2 levels in outer London'. E6 therefore overstates precision and loses the site-type restriction. It is the same origin as E1 and adds no independent support to A3 or A6. (conceded by proposer: E6 drops the 'roadside' and 'up to' qualifiers in E1 and shares its origin. It adds no independent support. The argument should rest on E1 alone.); C1 defeated_by: A3 is out because A27 (undercut) stands: [definitions] C1 claims roughly 1-3 µg/m3 or 3-10%. E1 states only an upper bound ('up to 4.8%'). With no central estimate, the record is consistent with any value from 0 to 4.8%, which includes C2's range. The record does not state C1. (conceded by proposer: E1 gives only an upper bound of 4.8%. It does not state a central estimate in the 1-3 µg/m3 or 3-10% range. The report's Appendix 3 would need to give a central estimate and interval.); C2 defeated_by: A2 is out because A24 (undermine) stands: The 1.056 µg/m3 is 4.8% of the 22 µg/m3 2024 outer London mean from E3. That mean pools roadside and urban background sites (E3 credibility notes). The 4.8% applies to roadside NO2, whose level is higher, so the absolute change is understated. Using it as evidence that the effect is under 1 µg/m3 (A2 → C2) is a unit mismatch. (conceded by proposer: E3 itself says the 22 µg/m3 mean pools roadside and background sites, so applying the 4.8% to it understates the roadside absolute change. E56 is a unit mismatch for roadside NO2. A roadside-only outer London mean would fix it.); C2 defeated_by: A2 is out because A25 (undermine) stands: E58 converts an ex-ante projection to µg/m3. That projection is 1.5% of all-site average NO2, based on a projected 6.9% cut in transport NOx emissions (E13). The operator's ex-post estimate of outer London NOx emissions is 14% lower (E5), about twice the projected cut. The 0.33 µg/m3 is therefore stale as an effect size, and it is not a roadside figure. (conceded by proposer: E58 converts the ex-ante 1.5% projection from E13. It is an all-site average and is stale next to the ex-post modelled 14% NOx emissions cut (E5). It is not a roadside effect size. An ex-post roadside concentration estimate would answer this.); C3 defeated_by: A1 is out because A18 (undercut) stands: [bias] Anticipation contaminates the comparison. The ULEZ3 pre-period runs from 19 July 2021 (E32), so it includes the Nov 2022 announcement and the Jan 2023 scrappage scheme. S1 says the impact 'started ahead of the formal start' (E4). Non-compliance fell from 23.1% to 7.4% before implementation (E27). A synthetic control fitted on a pre-period that already holds part of the treatment absorbs that part into the counterfactual. The post-29 Aug contrast is therefore biased towards zero, and 'no detectable impact' does not show the expansion had no effect. (conceded by proposer: E4 and E27 show the ULEZ3 pre-period (from 19 July 2021, E32) already contains anticipatory fleet change. E33 and E53 test anticipation only for ULEZ1. A null from this design cannot show the expansion had no effect. Answering this would need an anticipation placebo around the Nov 2022 announcement, or a pre-period ending before it.); C3 defeated_by: A1 is out because A23 (undermine) stands: The E22 text says 'the text elsewhere says outer-London NO2 changes were not significant'. That statement (E44/E25) concerns ULEZ1 in 2019, not ULEZ3. The quoted Fig. 3 caption covers only central and inner London. E22 provides no outer London ULEZ3 result, so its relevance to C3 is overstated. (conceded by proposer: The E44/E25 statement on non-significant outer London changes concerns ULEZ1. The Fig. 3 caption in E22 covers only central and inner London. E22 gives no outer London ULEZ3 result. Outer London ULEZ3 estimates from the supplementary tables would answer this.); C3 rebutted: rebuttal A21 stands: [precision] C3 asserts an effect of exactly zero. The independent study itself reports a further 2.7-4.7% fall in non-compliant vehicles after implementation, which the authors say is 'expected to lead to reduced NOx emissions' (E26/E43). The operator models outer London NOx emissions as 14% lower (E5). 'Not detectable' over about 3 months is not evidence of zero when the authors expect a reduction in the mechanism. (conceded by proposer: A null over about 3 months does not show an effect of exactly zero. E26 and E43 report a further fall in non-compliance, and the authors expect a NOx reduction. E5 models a 14% fall in outer London NOx emissions. C3's 'exactly zero' wording is too strong. At most the data fail to detect an effect.); C4 defeated_by: A4 is out because A32 (undermine) stands: E10 asserts that a no-ULEZ London cannot be 'accurately measured'. It gives no analysis. Independent researchers built exactly such a counterfactual from 60 non-London sites with weather normalisation (E18, E31). E10 is partisan assertion, not evidence of model dependence. A4, A10 and A13 should not rest on it. (conceded by proposer: E10 is a partisan assertion without analysis. E18 and E31 show a non-London counterfactual with weather normalisation was built. E10 should not support claims of model dependence. Evidence of divergence among methods would be needed.)
